findings.title: A definite pre-admission capacity rejection permanently consumed the configured native attempt
findings.observed_failure: evaluate set _attempted before awaiting the coordinator. A full coordinator rejected capacity without invoking acceptance. After pressure cleared, the next explicit call only inspected the original absent key and returned no_work, so this configured application could never start its otherwise unaccepted work.
failure_schedule: Hold four real public FixedPolicyCoordinator.find calls so max_active=4 is exhausted.
Call NativePolicyApplication.evaluate with its original frozen request and command.
Observe capacity_rejected=1, no Authority.submit call, no accepted record, no issued attempt and no specialist invocation.
Release all four held reads and wait for actual coordinator.pending_count=0.
Call evaluate explicitly again. Before repair it returns no_work; after repair it produces one result with the same binding/payload and one original command.

boundary_proof.claim: The coordinator resolves existing identity before acceptance and reconciles unknown commit by lookup, never by resubmitting.
Coordinator capacity rejects before a new call is admitted.
Public P1 executor-capacity rejection translates to WorkError(capacity).
Once entering the commit boundary, P1 maps a failure to acknowledgement_unknown rather than capacity.
Retained-identity capacity is checked before insertion; existing replay precedes this cap.

findings.repair: Reset only _attempted when CoordinatorError('capacity') is raised by the initial submit await. Keep the original request/command, _reserved/_submitting ownership accounting and all unknown/post-acceptance paths. This permits a later explicit call, never an automatic retry.

regression_tests.name: test_pre_admission_capacity_allows_explicit_same_request_retry
regression_tests.result: Failed before repair with no_work versus result; passed after repair.

regression_tests.name: test_unknown_submit_ack_never_retries_acceptance_or_issues
regression_tests.result: Committed-but-lost submit ACK plus failed reconciliation remains original-key lookup only; one submit, zero issues/invocations.

regression_tests.name: test_runner_capacity_after_acceptance_keeps_calls_lookup_only
regression_tests.result: Post-acceptance issue capacity remains lookup-only even after pressure clears; no second issuance/invocation.

findings.proof_limit: The new regressions use actual public P3 coordinator/runner with an in-memory public-authority fixture. P1 storage code establishes the error contract by review; an actual PG capacity/ACK failpoint rerun is not claimed.

findings.title: A valid remote contract rejection is reported by the runner as invalid_result
findings.evidence: The transport deliberately represents a valid delegation.error envelope as ContractError(code), including unauthorized/capacity. The runner catches ContractError from invoke_observed and always converts it to invalid_result. That conflates a correctly framed remote rejection with malformed or mismatched result bytes.
findings.safety: The path fails closed; it does not complete a result or authorize reinvocation. This is an operator-diagnosis/metric issue, not evidence of duplicate external execution.

source_test.name: test_known_safe_remote_errors_and_malformed_error_envelopes
source_test.claim: The transport test explicitly expects a valid unauthorized envelope to produce ContractError; reviewed, not rerun in this audit.

findings.recommendation: If addressed in a future authorized slice, preserve a finite safe remote-rejection classification distinct from result validation, without adding retry advice or changing P1 ownership.
findings.proof_limit: Source trace and existing transport test body, not a newly executed end-to-end regression.

findings.title: Five specialist child-fixture tests ran under a different exact Node patch version
findings.evidence: The parent TS log contains four standalone readiness failures and one durable fixed-policy readiness failure, with 183 specialist tests passing. Both fixture mains explicitly require process.versions.node === '24.22.2'. Current /opt/homebrew/bin/node reports v24.22.3; .node-version requires 24.22.2.
findings.reproduction: One standalone child was launched with valid synthetic role-closed environment and private 0700 paths. It exited 1 before creating readiness/endpoint files; stderr was empty and its sanitized stdout reported standalone_fixture_failed plus cleanup_complete:true. Actual process exit was awaited before removing its private directory.
findings.diagnosis: Setup guard rejection explains the affected readiness symptoms; the import-without-side-effects test passes. There is no evidence that rebuilding dist can change the exact runtime guard. Do not widen deadlines or weaken the guard to manufacture a pass.
findings.remedy: Parent fetched the official 24.22.2 darwin-arm64 archive, verified it against the official checksum manifest and used an isolated temporary binary. All 188 specialist tests in 11 files passed in 2.51 seconds; no runtime guard, system Node or repository pin changed.
findings.proof_limit: The initial standalone reproduction diagnosed setup failure. The subsequent full specialist suite passed under the exact pinned runtime in a parent-owned run whose saved log was inspected. This does not qualify actual PG, browser/media or provider lanes.

intentional_differences.title: Native conversational TaskGroup is not the durable P1 execution queue
intentional_differences.explanation: The baseline intentionally compares one tool and real SDK AgentTask/TaskGroup within a single session. Durable acceptance/issuance/results are supplied by the separate P1-backed facade. No SDK task, generic result annotation or model statement grants durable invocation or action authority.

intentional_differences.title: The implementation correctly uses the pinned Python task API rather than incompatible Academy examples
intentional_differences.explanation: Installed 1.8.11 takes task factories plus id/description, awaits the TaskGroup and exposes task_results. It does not accept the Academy's shown output_type, group.run(session) or summarize_between_tasks forms. P3 also explicitly validates the returned runtime PolicyResult because AgentTask.complete merely stores its Python value/exception.

intentional_differences.title: SDK waiter cancellation and durable business cancellation are intentionally separate
intentional_differences.explanation: CANCELLABLE allows the conversational waiter to stop. A shielded actual runner and its public owner's pending count remain retained; no automatic P1 cancellation is inferred. The focused actual-SDK test proves useful held-work continuation using scripted model and fake durable ports, not live media or provider behavior.

intentional_differences.title: Only newly created issuance followed by the exact fresh running grant permits HTTP invocation
intentional_differences.explanation: Issue ACK ambiguity reconciles the original command and returns a view; created=false does not invoke. A created grant is compared against a fresh running observation, cancellation and expiry before transport. Verified result truth is then recorded via public P1 completion; current case applicability is a separate read.

intentional_differences.title: Cross-principal result/cancel grants are an explicit trust-policy choice
intentional_differences.explanation: Historical P3-A9 is not an unauthenticated bypass: current scope/capability credentials are required. A distinct result principal and distinct cancel principal are deliberately tested. Binding observation/control exclusively to the starting principal would change this delegated-operations policy and needs an explicit design decision.

intentional_differences.title: Observer-owned telemetry resources do not extend server ownership
intentional_differences.explanation: Notifications are bounded/dropped rather than becoming an unbounded telemetry queue. The documented observer contract makes its external resources application-owned; successful server close is not a claim that arbitrary observer-created exporter I/O has closed.

intentional_differences.title: Late verified result truth, delivery receipt and exact action permission remain separate
intentional_differences.explanation: A stored eligible-at-commit result is historical P1 time/lease/cancel truth, not an evergreen action permit. Delivery uses immutable receiver intent and possible-send lookup semantics. Exact human confirmation and current atomic public P1 action guards remain separate from model tools.
